ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because the shelf is a crossroads: Honest Ned plus Old Dunmore replays any tribe's When played effect, and Grisel fields shelved Wenna, Sentry or Rufa copies that fire their own text, so every turn is a real hold-or-run puzzle.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because no tribe owns the shop and pool: a persistent shelf that ages, steals enemy kills, finishes triples and stocks spells plays unlike anything in Battlegrounds or a generic auto-battler.

verdict_why: One real clarity fix: what a Seized spell does on the shelf; the rest is ready for the owner to balance.

points.text: Officer Nyx can Seize the shop's spell, but the Customs House 'holds 3 units'. Say whether a spell takes a shelf place, and whether Grisel, Narrows Sentry, Wenna, the Stoker and the Auctioneer count or use it.

Gammer Eelby makes a buy-back net 0 gold (2 in, 1+1 out), so two free laundering passes a turn feed Creel-Bottom Kit and Nan's counter. That is a lovely hidden engine; worth naming in the free traders build so players find it.
Auctioneer Ardley eats the oldest, most-aged shelf unit that Grisel and the Bond Clerk want to keep. Good tension; a line in the builds on when to run both would show it is intended.
Two Honest Neds can launder each other for 2 gold a pass, each pass +2/+2 and a Pebble Jack trigger. Bounded by gold, and a fine Johnny discovery; keep it.
Tibby Slick is the one card that touches nothing else in the tribe. A Contraband or shelf hook (for example, a bought-back Tibby redirects twice) would pull it into the web.

standouts.why: Grisel turns the shelf into a second board, and copies of shelved Wenna, Sentry, Rufa or another tribe's fighters stack in ways the designer only half listed.
Honest Ned is the off-label key: launder your own unit to replay its When played effect, raise its sell price, and feed every Contraband payoff.
Corporal Rufa steals copies of what it kills, which the Bond Clerk ages, Grisel fields and the Keeper triples: an enemy-triple line no tribe has.

weakest.why: Tibby Slick's redirect is fine but sits outside both lanes.
Oilskin Molly is a plain end-of-turn buff to a tag; it does one obvious job.
Pebble Jack is a familiar 'after you play X, grow' scaler.

flags.note: A Seized spell's place and effect on the shelf is unstated.
Grisel with a shelved Wenna copy plus a real Wenna and the Keeper's fourth place can stack very high in one fight.
Golden Gammer Eelby makes each buy-back-and-sell a 1 gold profit, twice a turn, limited only by free Seizes.
